Accessibility is required for Viper Vision to work right.

1. Tap Open Accessibility → Installed apps → Viper Vision camera & screenshots. Tap it even if it's greyed out (otherwise the ⋮ in the next step won't be there). If it isn't greyed out, just turn it on and you're done.

2. Come back and tap App info → ⋮ (top right) → Allow restricted settings.

3. Come back, tap Open Accessibility again and turn Viper Vision camera & screenshots on.

Turn off Samsung's own screenshot toolbar:

Settings → Advanced features → Screenshots and screen recordings → turn off "Show toolbar after capturing".

Then come back here and take a screenshot (Power + Volume down) to check.

Viper Vision needs All files access to manage your photos and albums without Android asking every time: saving over originals, rotating, deleting, moving, and hidden albums.\n\nTap Open Settings and turn on \"Allow access to manage all files\".
✗ Samsung\'s toolbar is still on. Turn it off, then take another screenshot.

Are you really sure you want to restore all %1$d items?
%1$s for %2$d photo(s). Tap to delete them

This deletes the untouched copies kept of photos you\'ve edited or rotated (%1$s).\n\nYour photos stay exactly as they are now, but "Revert to original" will no longer be able to bring back how they looked before. This can\'t be undone.

This deletes the saved thumbnails, so photos and albums load more slowly for a while as they\'re made again, plus temporary files left over from editing (AI results and video previews).\n\nYour photos and videos, edits you\'ve saved, the recycle bin, downloaded AI models, the originals kept for "Revert to original" and your settings all stay.

It also needs Viper Vision\'s accessibility service on (the next screen), and Samsung\'s own screenshot toolbar off
